## Use the circle formula with centre (0, 0)
A circle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $r$ has equation $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$.
x^2 + y^2 &= 5^2
x^2 + y^2 &= 25
ANSWER: x^2 + y^2 = 25

## Substitute P(-4, k) into the equation of the circle
(-4)^2 + k^2 &= 25
16 + k^2 &= 25
k^2 &= 9
## Take the positive square root
$P$ is above the $x$-axis, so $k > 0$ and we reject $-3$.
k &= 3
ANSWER: k = 3

## Area of the semi-circle (radius 5)
A_{\text{semi}} &= \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2
&= \frac{1}{2}\pi (5)^2
&= \frac{25\pi}{2}
&\approx 39.2699
## Area of the triangle ABP
The base is $|AB| = 10$ and the height is $k = 3$.
A_{\triangle} &= \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 3
&= 15
## Subtract the triangle from the semi-circle
A_{\text{region}} &= 39.2699 - 15
&= 24.2699
&\approx 24.27
ANSWER: 24.27 \text{ square units}

## Find the slope of BC using B(6, 3) and C(5, 5)
m_{BC} &= \frac{5 - 3}{5 - 6}
&= \frac{2}{-1}
&= -2
## Write the equation using the point B(6, 3)
y - 3 &= -2(x - 6)
y - 3 &= -2x + 12
## Rearrange to the form ax + by + c = 0
2x + y - 3 &= 12
2x + y - 15 &= 0
ANSWER: 2x + y - 15 = 0

## Find |BD| using B(6, 3) and D(1, 3)
$ABCD$ is a rectangle, so triangle $ABD$ is right-angled at $A$, and $BD$ is the hypotenuse.
|BD| &= \sqrt{(6-1)^2 + (3-3)^2}
&= \sqrt{25}
&= 5
## Use sine: opposite over hypotenuse
The side opposite angle $ABD$ is $|AD| = \sqrt{5}$.
\sin ABD &= \frac{|AD|}{|BD|}
&= \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}
## Find the angle
\angle ABD &= \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\right)
&\approx 26.565^\circ
&\approx 27^\circ
ANSWER: \angle ABD \approx 27^\circ

## Draw a rough sketch first
Sides: $|AB| = 8$ cm, $|AC| = 5$ cm, $|BC| = 7$ cm.
## Draw the base AB
Use a ruler to draw a line segment $AB$ exactly 8 cm long.
## Mark C with two arcs
Set the compass to 5 cm, put the point on $A$ and draw an arc above $AB$.
Set the compass to 7 cm, put the point on $B$ and draw an arc that crosses the first.
Label the crossing point $C$.
## Join the vertices
Draw $AC$ and $BC$ with a ruler, and check the sides measure 5 cm and 7 cm.
ANSWER: \text{Triangle } ABC \text{ with } |AB|=8,\ |AC|=5,\ |BC|=7 \text{ cm}

## Area of a square is side times side
\text{Area} &= 2k \times 2k
&= 4k^2
ANSWER: 4k^2 \text{ cm}^2

## Use Pythagoras to find k
The removed triangle has legs 20 and 20, and hypotenuse $2k$.
(2k)^2 &= 20^2 + 20^2
4k^2 &= 400 + 400
4k^2 &= 800
k^2 &= 200
## Take the positive square root
k &= \sqrt{200}
&= 10\sqrt{2}
&\approx 14.14
## Area of the square
4k^2 &= 4 \times 200
&= 800
## Area of the removed triangle
\tfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 20 &= 200
## Subtract to get the shaded area
\text{Shaded} &= 800 - 200
&= 600
ANSWER: k \approx 14.14, \quad \text{shaded area} = 600 \text{ cm}^2

## The mean goes in the middle
The centre of a normal curve is the mean, so the middle box is 100.
## Add the standard deviation (15) going right
100 + 15 &= 115
115 + 15 &= 130
130 + 15 &= 145
## Subtract the standard deviation (15) going left
100 - 15 &= 85
85 - 15 &= 70
70 - 15 &= 55
The 85 box was already given, which checks the pattern.
ANSWER: 55,\ 70,\ 85,\ 100,\ 115,\ 130,\ 145

## (ii) Scores between 70 and 130
$70 = 100 - 2(15)$ and $130 = 100 + 2(15)$, so this is within 2 standard deviations of the mean.
The Empirical Rule says about 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations.
P(70 < X < 130) &= 0.95
## (iii) Scores between 85 and 115
$85 = 100 - 15$ and $115 = 100 + 15$, so this is within 1 standard deviation of the mean.
The Empirical Rule says about 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation.
\text{Number} &= 0.68 \times 1200
&= 816
ANSWER: \text{(ii) } 0.95 \qquad \text{(iii) } 816 \text{ people}

## Count the pupils who are boys or do not study chemistry
Pupils who study chemistry: $6 + 9 = 15$, so $24 - 15 = 9$ do not.
Boys: 10. Girls who do not study chemistry: $14 - 9 = 5$.
\text{Favourable} &= 10 + 5
&= 15
## Probability = favourable over total
P &= \frac{15}{24}
ANSWER: \frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}

## Find the third angle
Angles in a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
180 - 65 - 63 &= 52
## Write the sine rule
$x$ is opposite the $52^\circ$ angle and $10$ is opposite the $63^\circ$ angle.
\frac{x}{\sin 52^\circ} &= \frac{10}{\sin 63^\circ}
## Solve for x
Multiply both sides by $\sin 52^\circ$.
x &= \frac{10 \sin 52^\circ}{\sin 63^\circ}
With the calculator in degree mode, $10\sin 52^\circ \approx 7.880$ and $\sin 63^\circ \approx 0.8910$.
x &= 8.84
ANSWER: x = 8.84\text{ cm}

## Write the cosine rule
Two sides and the angle between them are known, so use the cosine rule for the side opposite that angle.
y^2 &= 8.5^2 + 10.2^2 - 2(8.5)(10.2)\cos 53.8^\circ
## Work out the numbers
8.5^2 &= 72.25
10.2^2 &= 104.04
2(8.5)(10.2) &= 173.4
## Substitute and add
y^2 &= 72.25 + 104.04 - 173.4\cos 53.8^\circ
y^2 &= 176.29 - 173.4\cos 53.8^\circ
## Evaluate with the calculator
In degree mode, $\cos 53.8^\circ \approx 0.59057$.
y^2 &= 73.88
## Take the square root
A length is positive, so take the positive root.
y &= \sqrt{73.88}
y &= 8.60
ANSWER: y = 8.60\text{ cm}

## Use height = diameter
The diameter is twice the radius.
h &= 2r
h &= 2(2.25)
h &= 4.5
ANSWER: h = 4.5\text{ m}

## Use Pythagoras on the cone
The height, radius and slant height form a right-angled triangle with $l$ as the hypotenuse.
l^2 &= h^2 + r^2
l^2 &= 4.5^2 + 2.25^2
l^2 &= 20.25 + 5.0625
l^2 &= 25.3125
## Take the square root
l &= \sqrt{25.3125}
l &= 5.03
ANSWER: l = 5.03\text{ m}

## Curved surface area of 14 cones
The curved surface area of one cone is $\pi r l$.
\text{CSA} &= 14\pi r l
&= 14 \times \pi (2.25)(5.03)
&= 497.77
ANSWER: 497.77\text{ m}^2

## Find the number of containers
Each container holds 5 litres, so divide 41 by 5.
\frac{41}{5} &= 8.2
## Round up to whole containers
You cannot buy part of a container, and 8 would not be enough, so round up.
\text{Containers} &= 9
## Find the cost in Australian dollars
Each container costs 110 Australian dollars.
9 \times 110 &= 990
## Convert to euro
The cost is 990 Australian dollars. Multiply by 0.68.
990 \times 0.68 &= \text{€}673.20
&\approx \text{€}673
ANSWER: 9\text{ containers, cost } \text{€}673

## Find the arc length p
The arc of the sector wraps around the base of the cone, so it equals the circumference of the base (radius 2.25).
p &= 2\pi r
&= 2\pi (2.25)
&= 14.14
## Write the arc length as a fraction of the full circle
The sector has radius 5.03, so its full circle has circumference $2\pi(5.03)$.
p &= \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi (5.03)
14.14 &= \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi (5.03)
## Solve for theta
\theta &= \frac{14.14 \times 360}{2\pi (5.03)}
&= 161.07
&\approx 161
ANSWER: p = 14.14\text{ m}, \quad \theta = 161^\circ

## Read each point from the grid
Read across to the $x$-value, then up or down to the $y$-value. Write each as $(x, y)$.
A &= (1, -2)
B &= (4, 2)
D &= (6, -6)
E &= (15, 6)
ANSWER: A = (1,-2),\ B = (4,2),\ D = (6,-6),\ E = (15,6)

## Move A to the origin
Subtract $A(1,-2)$ from each point, so $A$ becomes $(0,0)$.
B &\to (4-1,\ 2-(-2)) = (3, 4)
C &\to (4.5-1,\ 0-(-2)) = (3.5, 2)
## Use the area formula
With one vertex at the origin, area $= \tfrac12 |x_1 y_2 - x_2 y_1|$.
\text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2}|(3)(2) - (3.5)(4)|
&= \frac{1}{2}|6 - 14|
&= \frac{1}{2}|-8|
&= \frac{1}{2}(8)
&= 4
ANSWER: \text{Area} = 4\text{ square units}

## Areas scale by the square of the scale factor
Lengths are multiplied by $k$, so areas are multiplied by $k^2$.
\text{Area } CDE &= k^2 \times \text{Area } CBA
&= 3^2 \times 4
&= 9 \times 4
&= 36
ANSWER: 36\text{ square units}

## Subtract the valid votes from the total votes
Total votes = valid votes + invalid or blank votes.
33\,577\,342 - 33\,551\,983 &= 25\,359
## Fill in the table
Write $25\,359$ in the "Invalid or blank votes" row of Table 1.
ANSWER: 25\,359

## Leave votes as a fraction of valid votes
Use the valid votes, not the total votes.
\frac{17\,410\,742}{33\,551\,983} \times 100 &= 51.89
&\approx 52
ANSWER: 52\%

## Choose the chart
Two percentages for each of six age groups: a bar chart with the Remain and Leave bars side by side for each group lets you compare them.
## Draw the axes
Put the age groups along the horizontal axis. Put the percentage on the vertical axis, from 0 to 80.
## Draw the bars
For each age group draw a blue Remain bar and a red Leave bar, with heights taken from Table 2. Add a key.
ANSWER: \text{Clustered bar chart of Table 2}

## Explain the problem
The means treat every age group as equal, but the groups did not have equal numbers of voters.
Table 2 gives percentages only. The number of voters in each age group is not used, so the means are unreliable.
The real result (Table 1) was Leave 52%, so the Remain mean of 52.33% does not reflect the outcome.
ANSWER: \text{The number of voters in each age group is not used, so the means are unreliable.}

## Use the margin of error formula
Margin of error $= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ with $n = 1200$.
\frac{1}{\sqrt{1200}} &= 0.02887
&= 2.887\%
&\approx 3\%
ANSWER: 3\%

## Find the sample proportion as a percentage
\hat{p} &= \frac{578}{1200} \times 100
&= 48.17
## Add and subtract the margin of error
The confidence interval is $\hat{p} \pm$ margin of error.
48.17 - 3 < p &< 48.17 + 3
45.17 < p &< 51.17
ANSWER: 45.17\% < p < 51.17\%

## State the hypotheses
H_0 &: p = 53\%
H_1 &: p \ne 53\%
## Compare the claim with the confidence interval
The 95% confidence interval is $45\% < p < 51\%$. The claimed value $53\%$ is not inside it.
## Conclude in context
Reject $H_0$ at the 5% level. There is evidence that the party's claim that 53% of the Irish population think the UK leaving the EU would hurt the Irish economy is false.
ANSWER: \text{Reject } H_0\text{: the party's claim is false}

## Label the equations and plan to eliminate y
Call the equations (i), (ii) and (iii). Equation (iii) has no $y$, so eliminate $y$ from (i) and (ii) to get a second equation in $x$ and $z$.
\text{(i)}\quad 2x + 3y - z &= -4
\text{(ii)}\quad 3x + 2y + 2z &= 14
\text{(iii)}\quad x - 3z &= -13
## Multiply (i) by 2 and (ii) by -3
4x + 6y - 2z &= -8
-9x - 6y - 6z &= -42
## Add the two equations to eliminate y
-5x - 8z &= -50
## Multiply (iii) by 5
5x - 15z &= -65
## Add to eliminate x and find z
-5x - 8z &= -50
5x - 15z &= -65
-23z &= -115
z &= \frac{-115}{-23}
z &= 5
## Substitute z = 5 into (iii) to find x
x - 3(5) &= -13
x - 15 &= -13
x &= 2
## Substitute x = 2 and z = 5 into (i) to find y
2(2) + 3y - 5 &= -4
3y - 1 &= -4
3y &= -3
y &= -1
ANSWER: x = 2,\; y = -1,\; z = 5

## Multiply both sides by (x + 2)^2
$(x+2)^2$ is always positive (as $x \ne -2$), so the inequality sign does not change.
\frac{2x-3}{x+2} &\ge 3
(2x-3)(x+2) &\ge 3(x+2)^2
## Expand both sides
2x^2 + 4x - 3x - 6 &\ge 3(x^2 + 4x + 4)
2x^2 + x - 6 &\ge 3x^2 + 12x + 12
## Collect all terms on one side
0 &\ge 3x^2 - 2x^2 + 12x - x + 12 + 6
0 &\ge x^2 + 11x + 18
x^2 + 11x + 18 &\le 0
## Factorise to find the roots
(x+2)(x+9) &\le 0
The roots are $x = -2$ and $x = -9$.
## Choose the values between the roots
The product of two brackets is negative or zero only between the roots, since the $x^2$ coefficient is positive.
-9 &\le x \le -2
The original fraction is undefined at $x = -2$, so exclude it.
-9 &\le x < -2
ANSWER: -9 \le x < -2

## Set the two common ratios equal
In a geometric series, $\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{T_3}{T_2}$.
\frac{5x-8}{x^2} &= \frac{x+8}{5x-8}
## Cross-multiply
(5x-8)^2 &= x^2(x+8)
## Expand both sides
(5x-8)(5x-8) &= x^3 + 8x^2
25x^2 - 80x + 64 &= x^3 + 8x^2
## Move every term to one side
0 &= x^3 + 8x^2 - 25x^2 + 80x - 64
0 &= x^3 - 17x^2 + 80x - 64
x^3 - 17x^2 + 80x - 64 &= 0
ANSWER: x^3 - 17x^2 + 80x - 64 = 0

## Substitute x = 1 into f(x)
f(1) &= (1)^3 - 17(1)^2 + 80(1) - 64
&= 1 - 17 + 80 - 64
&= 0
So $f(1) = 0$, which means $(x-1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$.
## Split the terms so (x - 1) can be taken out
f(x) &= x^3 - 17x^2 + 80x - 64
&= x^3 - x^2 - 16x^2 + 80x - 64
&= x^2(x-1) - 16x^2 + 80x - 64
&= x^2(x-1) - 16x^2 + 16x + 64x - 64
&= x^2(x-1) - 16x(x-1) + 64x - 64
&= x^2(x-1) - 16x(x-1) + 64(x-1)
&= (x-1)(x^2 - 16x + 64)
## Solve the quadratic factor
Set $f(x) = 0$. The factor $(x-1)$ gives $x = 1$, so look at the quadratic.
x^2 - 16x + 64 &= 0
(x-8)(x-8) &= 0
x &= 8
ANSWER: x = 8
